feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence so far: iteration 0 (baseline, 0.12 m track, ±0.024 m array, 0.6 kg) finished the oval 20/20 at 1.65 s with oscillation 0.15, but the s-bend and slalom went off track at progress 0.17 and 0.12 with max_error about 0.061 m, at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 1 (±0.032 m array, 0.10 m track, 0.033 m radius, 0.5 kg, kp 2.8, kd 0.4) finished only 17/20 on the oval, slowed to 1.84 s, raised oscillation to 0.26, and improved the bends only partly (s-bend 0.24, slalom 0.19). The array widening looks useful; the narrower track and drivetrain change look harmful. For the controller I kept the weights in sensor order and returned kp and kd to the baseline values, because the higher gains were tied to the narrower track. Next race decides the next change. If the s-bend or slalom still go off track with max_error near 0.06 m and the oval finishes, the limit is likely sensor lead or footprint: try sensor y 0.03 or sensor_size 0.016. If the oval finishes but steering_oscillation rises well above 0.15 on the oval, the 0.5 kg mass is probably too light for this controller: return to 0.6 kg. If the oval stops finishing, return the drivetrain fully to baseline and keep the wider array.
requested_changes: If the s-bend or slalom still end off track with line_loss_events of 1 or more and max_error near 0.06 m, change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 so the 16 mm pitch leaves no gaps across the 25 mm tape. Iteration 0 gave max_error 0.061 on both bends, and iteration 1 showed the wider array helps progress (0.17 to 0.24), so coverage is the open question.

If the oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 (baseline 0.15, iteration 1 0.26) while the array is wide, change mass from 0.5 back to 0.6 kg. Iteration 1 used 0.5 kg with the narrower track, so the mass effect was never isolated.

If sensor coverage is confirmed but the bends still fail, move the sensor row from y 0.05 to y 0.03 to reduce the forward lead. Iteration 0's 50 mm lead gave bends with max_error at the limit, but no run has yet tested the lead on its own.
